001package io.jstach.rainbowgum.format;
002
003import org.eclipse.jdt.annotation.Nullable;
004
005/**
006 * Detects whether the current process is attached to an ANSI capable terminal so that
007 * formatters (e.g. the pattern module's color keywords) can decide whether to emit ANSI
008 * escape codes in the first place instead of emitting and later stripping them.
009 * <p>
010 * This uses only {@link System#console()} and well known environment variables and thus
011 * requires no native code or third party terminal library. On JDK versions prior to 22
012 * {@link System#console()} returns <code>null</code> whenever either standard in or
013 * standard out is redirected which is a safe (if slightly conservative) signal to disable
014 * ANSI output.
015 */
016public final class AnsiSupport {
017
018        private AnsiSupport() {
019        }
020
021        /**
022         * Determines if ANSI escape codes are likely supported by the current process's
023         * standard output.
024         * @return true if ANSI output should be emitted.
025         */
026        @SuppressWarnings("SystemConsoleNull")
027        public static boolean isAnsiSupported() {
028                if (System.console() == null) {
029                        return false;
030                }
031                return isAnsiSupported(System.getenv("NO_COLOR"), System.getenv("TERM"));
032        }
033
034        static boolean isAnsiSupported(@Nullable String noColor, @Nullable String term) {
035                if (noColor != null) {
036                        /*
037                         * https://no-color.org/ - presence of the variable disables color regardless
038                         * of value.
039                         */
040                        return false;
041                }
042                if ("dumb".equals(term)) {
043                        return false;
044                }
045                return true;
046        }
047
048}
